prompt.text: Start in workspace.ipynb, which contains the instructions and questions. This activity works for 1 to 4 people. I will post one personal Paper tutor link for each participant: open your own link on this laptop, then scan its QR code with your phone. Use this JupyterLab chat for paper done, coding done, and submitted.

Phase 1: work on the three paper questions in the notebook for up to 30 minutes. Think through the matrices, eligibility rule, selected entries, and running average, discussing with others if present, before writing code. Use your camera and individual chat for paper feedback. If working alone, type exactly paper done here; in a group, each member types it when ready to move on, or paper not done to withdraw readiness. Start coding only when I announce Phase 2.

Phase 2 starts now: you have up to 40 minutes. Stop camera capture and use your paper to implement Parts A and B in the notebook. Both parts are already available. If working alone, implement both functions yourself. In a group, coordinate who edits each function. Save before running each check and keep the supplied cell tags. When both checks pass and you have finished the debugging note, type exactly coding done here. In a group, everyone must type it; alone, your own message is sufficient. Use coding not done to withdraw readiness.

The coding phase has ended, either because everyone present was ready with both checks passed or because the 40 minutes elapsed. Save your current work, including any unfinished code. If working alone, run the final submission cell with your activity email. In a group, choose one person to submit for everyone. Wait for a submission ID, then type submitted here. The ID confirms storage. Keep it; your instructor can see the final score.
Thanks for confirming submission. Keep your submission ID. Your instructor can see your stored notebook and final grade. Keep your paper notes for the instructor. This concludes the activity.
